$comment: THE canonical shared authority contract for Admin and Partner Portal.
There is deliberately NO cross-repository runtime import. Two surfaces that must agree
are kept in agreement by a shared SPECIFICATION plus shared CONFORMANCE VECTORS, both
held here, and executed against every implementation by
scripts/shared-authority-contract-verify.mjs. A runtime import across lane boundaries
would couple deploy artifacts and let one lane's refactor silently change another lane's
authorization; a contract with executable vectors detects drift without that coupling.
Implementations are listed under `implementations`. Adding a surface means adding it
there — an implementation that is not listed is not verified, and the verifier fails if
v2.0.0 closes the role vocabulary. Previously any non-empty string was a role, so a
principal hired as "intern" passed every privileged gate. CANONICAL_ADMIN_ROLES is now
an explicit, versioned allowlist and vectors V24-V26 change verdict accordingly — they
used to assert that case-variant roles were staff, which was the defect written down.

statusNormalization.rationale: Folds only canonically equivalent spellings. Confusables (Cyrillic А, fullwidth Ａ) are different strings under NFC and therefore remain refused, which is correct: a value that merely looks right is not right.
statusNormalization.note: toLowerCase is locale-invariant in JS. Turkish dotted/dotless I produces a false NEGATIVE (denial), never a false positive.

acceptedStatuses.derivation: The only status ever written: the hire-staff callable writes 'Active'; setEmployeeStatus refuses any value other than 'Active' or 'Suspended' before writing.
acceptedStatuses.widening: Adding a value here widens who may act as platform staff and is a reviewed change, never incidental.

roleComparison.derivation: Derived, not invented: 'Director' is the master gate in the hire-staff and set-status callables; 'Manager' and 'Support' are the only options the HR console offers. No other value is written to admin_users anywhere in the repository.

foreignVocabularies.rule: A partner_memberships role is a DIFFERENT principal class and must never satisfy an Admin gate.

roleComparison.rationale: Case-folding, trimming or normalizing a role WIDENS authority — "director" would begin to grant Director powers it has never had. Hardening must not widen. A non-canonical spelling fails closed and the migration dry-run reports it, so the record is corrected rather than the predicate.
roleComparison.widening: Adding a role means bumping registryVersion and updating these vectors and the migration classifier together.

principalBinding.source: request.auth.uid, verified by the Functions runtime
principalBinding.roleSource: admin_users/{uid}, read server-side inside the transaction where one exists
forbidden: reading identity, role, status or authorization claims from request.data
accepting a published surrogate reference as an identity
principalBinding.rule: Status is evaluated BEFORE role. A valid role can never rescue an inactive account.

suspensionBehaviour.appliesTo: every privileged call site, including the callables that create or modify staff
suspensionBehaviour.knownConsequence: If every Director record is inactive or status-less, there is no in-product recovery path. This is intentional (no break-glass) and is why the status migration verifier must run before activation.

cacheDisposal.trigger: any change to the authority fingerprint
cacheDisposal.rationale: Content scoped to an identity at a moment stops being authorized the instant that identity changes. Retaining it is a disclosure, not a cache.

commandRetirement.idScope: one stable id per user INTENT (draft, decision, expected version, content reference)
commandRetirement.retainedOn: transport failure, timeout, or any outcome where the server's decision is unknown
commandRetirement.singleFlight: separate from reservation — a failed attempt must still permit a retry
commandRetirement.rationale: Retiring an id on a transport failure mints a new id on retry, which applies an accepted-but-response-lost command a second time.

auditEvidence.immutability: append-only; create-only writes, never update or delete

implementations.consumers: all Admin and Portal privileged callables
Admin portal shell and client surfaces
implementations.note: Rendering decisions only. The server re-derives authority on every callable; nothing here grants anything.

conformanceVectors.$comment: Executed against EVERY implementation. `staff` and `director` are the required verdicts. Drift between implementations is a gate failure.

cases.note: MISSING status — the legacy shape the old denylist admitted
role case is NOT folded; with a closed registry a non-canonical spelling is not staff at all
uppercase is a different string and therefore a different, unrecognized role
a trailing space is a different role; previously this was staff because any non-empty string was
THE regression: a principal hired as intern passed every privileged gate
partner_memberships vocabulary must not satisfy an Admin gate
partner role, lowercase — neither canonical nor this principal class
Cyrillic о confusable in the role
status still beats a canonical role

driftDetection.method: Every implementation is executed against every conformance vector; any disagreement between an implementation and the contract, or between two implementations, fails the gate.
alsoChecks: the accepted-status list is identical in every implementation
the normalizers agree on every vector plus non-string inputs
no implementation has gained an accepted status the contract does not list
the canonical role registry is identical in every implementation
no canonical role is also listed as obsolete
no partner_memberships role appears in the admin registry
